name: Tundavala Gap
subtitle: Tundavala Gap (Fenda da Tundavala) is a deep gorge cut into the western edge of the Humpata plateau, in the Serra da Chela near Lubango in south-west Angola.

facts.label: Setting
facts.value: Serra da Chela near Lubango (Huíla Province), whose summit is the Humpata plateau

facts.label: Distance and coordinates
facts.value: Viewpoint and gap about 20 km from Lubango, at 13º22’S 14º49’E

facts.label: Height of the escarpment
facts.value: Described as an enormous escarpment of more than 1,000 m height, cut in igneous rocks

facts.label: Plateau elevation
facts.value: Highest points of the plateau edge near the gap: 2,326 to 2,330 m

facts.label: Geological setting
facts.value: One of several similar escarpments on the Humpata plateau edges, marking the limits of an intracratonic sedimentary basin of Paleo-Mesoproterozoic age on the Congo Craton

facts.label: Type locality
facts.value: Type locality of the Tundavala Formation, one of five formations of the Chela Group

facts.label: Chela Group
facts.value: The Chela Group comprises five formations

facts.label: Protection proposal
facts.value: The 2012 assessment was needed to support scientifically a proposal to classify the territory and preserve its physical integrity

facts.label: Cultural meaning
facts.value: Each of the peoples living around Tundavala interprets the landscape culturally in a different way

parts.text: Tundavala Gap (Fenda da Tundavala) is a deep gorge cut into the western edge of the Humpata plateau, in the Serra da Chela near Lubango in south-west Angola. Geologists describe an escarpment more than 1,000 metres high and the type locality of the Tundavala Formation of the Chela Group. A 2012 Portuguese-Angolan study assessed its geological heritage as a basis for a proposal to classify and protect it.
